channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Atlassian launches AMP: the Agentic Multiplayer Protocol that gives AI agents an identity on your team
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At Team '26 Europe in Amsterdam, Atlassian unveiled AMP — a framework that gives workplace AI agents an assigned identity, scoped authority, shared Teamwork Graph context and reviewable output — alongside a rebuilt Atlassian MCP server with 220+ tools, now generally available.

item.title: Ray Dalio says AI is ‘a classic bubble’ nearing its burst — debt, not the models, sets the clock
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Speaking at the Forbes Global CEO Conference in Singapore on Wednesday, the Bridgewater founder argued that the AI buildout is increasingly financed with debt, that rising bond yields are raising the cost of data centers and chips, and that “we’re close to” the bursting point — even as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 hit record highs.

item.title: Musk opens Grok Bot to rival models: Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney and Suno will power SpaceX's agent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Elon Musk announced on October 7 that Grok Bot, SpaceX’s persistent AI agent, will route each task to whichever backend model or API performs best — naming rival Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney and Suno. The post passed 3.8 million views, marking a striking multi-model turn for a lab that trains its own frontier models.

item.title: Beyond Now launches an agentic revenue platform for telecoms: native agents that package, sell and bill AI by token and outcome
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Beyond Now launched its Agentic Revenue & Ecosystem Orchestration Platform on October 7, betting that telecoms' AI problem is commercial, not technical: carriers have captured just 2% of AI revenue so far, CEO Angus Ward says, and the missing piece is a revenue stack built for an economy where agents — not humans — do the buying.

item.title: MedScout launches Scout AI: a MedTech rep's whole day done in seconds — and an MCP that plugs its market data into Claude, Copilot, Gemini and ChatGPT
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MedScout launched Scout AI on October 7: an AI that turns its claims-based market data into target lists, meeting briefs and optimized daily routes for MedTech sales reps in seconds — plus a Model Context Protocol server that plugs the same governed data into Claude, Copilot, Gemini and ChatGPT.

item.title: Stop hand-writing agent skills: let Claude Code learn its own — hands-on with AutoHarness
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AutoHarness (tigerless-labs/autoharness, ~9.1K stars, MIT) is a self-learning skill layer for Claude Code: it watches your real sessions, distills the lessons into native skills, merges the near-duplicates, and prunes the ones you never use — no daemon, no benchmark. Here is the full hands-on walkthrough, plus the honest trade-offs.

item.title: Cortex Discover 1.1.0: Pervaziv's agentic AI browser uses 36.7% less memory than Chrome, six-browser study finds
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Pervaziv AI published benchmark results for Cortex Discover 1.1.0, its dedicated agentic AI browser, ranking it first in memory and CPU efficiency across Chrome, Safari, Brave, Edge and Firefox — with throughput and rendering near-identical to Chrome. The company also disclosed where the browser still trails.

item.title: UK accepts all 44 AI-in-healthcare recommendations, ending one-off device approvals
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The UK government will accept all 44 recommendations from the NHS-doctors-led AI Commission: AI medical devices get lifecycle-long monitoring instead of one-off approvals, and the MHRA has opened applications for Phase 3 of its AI Airlock sandbox.

item.title: Google launches Nano Banana 2.1: sharper image edits at half the price — and a three-week shutdown notice
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google on Tuesday released Nano Banana 2.1, its latest image generation and editing model — roughly half the price of Nano Banana 2, ahead on every benchmark Google published, and already rolling out to the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Developers on the old model have until October 29 to switch.

item.title: Stop parsing JSON from your LLM: typed decisions with real probabilities — hands-on with AnyJev
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AnyJev (nokia-applied-research/AnyJev, ~1,100 stars, Apache-2.0) turns any open LLM into a decision engine: give it a state and a typed question — a choice, a yes/no, or a score — and read the answer as a probability distribution over the options, straight from the model's next-token distribution. Nothing generated, nothing parsed. Here is the full hands-on walkthrough, plus the honest trade-offs.

item.title: AlphaSense’s next-gen SuperAnalyst: the ‘always-on’ agent that monitors your thesis and rebuilds the deck itself
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AlphaSense launched a next-generation SuperAnalyst on Tuesday — an always-on AI agent for finance teams that plans research, runs the analysis, monitors the assumptions behind an investment thesis, and updates the work product on its own. The release adds a Context Graph, reusable Skills, and a preview of no-code SuperAnalyst Apps.

item.title: Anthropic opens Claude Mythos 5.1 to vetted defenders — and authorized hackers: the Cyber Verification Program's three tiers
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic merged Project Glasswing and its Cyber Verification Program into a single three-tier program announced Tuesday, giving verified security professionals reduced safeguards on Claude Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — after Glasswing partners found more than 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities in four months.

item.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Google DeepMind's 740M open model brings multimodal search to your phone, fully offline
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google DeepMind launched EmbeddingGemma 2, a 740-million-parameter open model that maps text, code, images, video and audio into one shared embedding space — small enough to run entirely on-device under the Apache 2.0 license.

item.title: Sierra and Meta launch the Personal Agent Protocol: open rules so your AI agent can shop, book, and pay
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sierra, Meta, Walmart, Stripe, Shopify, Instinct, Rocket and Genesys unveiled the Personal Agent Protocol — an open standard for how personal AI agents authenticate and transact with businesses. A v0.1 spec is planned for later this month.

item.title: Chatbots inform voters as well as Google: a 2,858-person PNAS Nexus trial finds AI no worse for political knowledge
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Published online today in PNAS Nexus, the study by Luettgau, Kirk, Hackenburg and colleagues had UK voters research claims on climate, immigration, criminal justice and COVID-19 policy using GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, Mistral or Google search. Belief in true information rose and belief in misinformation fell equally across every method — and the chatbot users finished 6–10% faster.

item.title: Melius raises $25M for the first ‘agents lab’ for creative work: AI agents take the production busywork
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Melius announced $25 million in total funding — a $5M seed led by General Catalyst and a $20M Series A led by CRV — to build what it calls the first ‘agents lab’ for creative work: a shared operating system where teams of AI agents handle the busywork of building images, video, and audio.

item.title: Give your coding agents an org chart: hands-on with Paperclip, the 98K-star agent orchestrator
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Paperclip (paperclipai/paperclip, ~98,000 stars, MIT) is a self-hosted Node.js server and React UI that turns your coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Cursor — into an org chart with goals, budgets, and approval gates. One command installs it; here is the full walkthrough, plus the honest trade-offs.

item.title: Anthropic bids for founders: a free year of Claude Team, $1,000 in API credits, and a $45K partner stack
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic expanded its Claude for Startups program during SF Tech Week: a one-time $1,000 API credit, a free year of Claude Team, and up to $45,000 in partner discounts and credits via a new Claude Startup Stack.

item.title: Infor expands Industry AI as survey finds generic AI falls short for two in three businesses
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Infor unveiled an expanded Industry AI architecture and the next evolution of its Velocity Suite at Velocity Week in Orlando, paired with a 2,111-firm survey: 68% of business leaders say off-the-shelf AI doesn't adequately address their industry's needs.

item.title: Boost Run lands $525.6M AI compute deal with an unnamed sovereign AI company — backlog tops $2.6B
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Boost Run announced a five-year, $525.6M AI cloud services deal with a leading sovereign AI company, powered by NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems, lifting its total contracted backlog past $2.6 billion.

item.title: AI may be hacking South Korea's banks: Lee orders a full investigation after 68,000 customers hit
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: President Lee Jae-myung said on Tuesday there are signs AI was used in recent bank hacks that exposed customer data across more than seven institutions, and ordered police and regulators into a full-scale investigation.

item.title: Mistral launches 'Le Chonk': a 1.05T-parameter open-weight model aimed at China's best — weights land October 27
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Mistral announced Mistral Large 4 — codename “Le Chonk” — on October 6: an open-weight, multimodal MoE with 49B active and 1.05T total parameters. CEO Arthur Mensch says it beats Chinese open models “including cyber”. Preview via API today; weights go public October 27.

item.title: Fujitsu puts four AI agents on the shop floor: retail trial starts today, seven chains in, full launch June 2027
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fujitsu announced a trial environment for four retail AI agents — sales structure analysis, customer loyalty, sales planning, and store-manager support — plus the execution platform that runs them, with demonstration experiments at seven retail companies and a full launch slated for June 2027.

item.title: Make your coding agent answer with pages, not walls of text: a hands-on guide to the Answer me with HTML skill
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Answer me with HTML (QingYunA/answer-me-with-html, 1,600+ stars, MIT) is an agent skill that turns your coding agent's explanations into readable HTML pages — sequence diagrams, comparison tables, even 3Blue1Brown-style explainer videos — while the model writes 6x fewer output tokens. Here is the one-command install, the settings that matter, and the honest trade-offs.

item.title: WhiteLab Genomics raises €23.2M to design genomic medicines that actually work in vivo — its ALFRED AI platform is winning Sanofi deals
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Paris biotech WhiteLab Genomics closed a €23.2 million ($26 million) Series B led by AVP on Tuesday to scale its ALFRED platform, which uses AI to design gene-therapy delivery vehicles — AAVs and lipid nanoparticles — then validates them in living systems. Roughly 15 pharma partnerships, including Sanofi, are already paying for it.
